notes.drawing: The written side of a postcard: message lines on the left, a divider, the stamp and one address line on the right. The card is the rectangle of Phosphor's envelope (x 32 to 224, y 56 to 200, corner radius 8); the envelope's flap lines are not part of it, so there is no frame check. Every gap is 16 units in regular.
notes.bold: The divider moves left to x 116 and the message lines get shorter, so the stamp can grow from 32 to 40 units and keep an opening; it also sits 4 units lower, and the address line follows. At the regular positions the stamp closed up and touched the divider.
notes.fill: The stamp is cut out as a solid square, as Phosphor's fills do with small frames.
